title: Compass of Forgotten Worlds
tagline: Four sealed rooms. One brass compass. Five minutes before the storm tide.

ui.noTruths: No chart notes yet. Finish a room to learn one.
ui.holdHelp: Now tap the right spot in the room.
ui.needItem: You need something for this. Check your Satchel.
ui.hintDone: Nothing left to solve here. Take the way out.

mission.kicker: The Map House, a stormy night
mission.heading: Compass of Forgotten Worlds
paras: Cartographer Aurelio Vance has vanished, leaving only his Map House and a brass compass that points to worlds erased from every map.
You are Tamsin, his apprentice, and Corvin, the airship boy, is at your side. Four sealed rooms lie between you and the truth.
Open them before the storm tide floods the house. You have five minutes.

tutorial.text: Drag to look around. Glowing lights can be tapped.
Things you find go into your Satchel. Clues go into your Logbook. Open it any time.
Every room ends with one puzzle. Close it any time with the X. Wrong answers cost Bearings.
You have 3 hints for the whole game, each costs 25 Bearings. Watch the clock: the tide rises in five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: aurelio
dialogue.text: Tamsin, if you hear this, I could not stay. The compass is yours now. Open the four rooms before the tide rises, and learn what I hid from the maps.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: He is really gone. But he left the compass, and it points at nothing on any map.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Then we follow it. I will watch the storm, you watch the rooms. Let us go.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Let us look around again. Something is catching the light.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Master Aurelio's study. Every map here is blank, as if the names were rubbed out.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Blank maps and a storm outside. Let us see what he left on the desk.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The dial clicked! The bookcase is sliding open.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Aurelio wrote the bearings down: West, South, East. And he says the Eye and the Flame are not in the code.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The letter is written backwards. Aurelio's brass plate must show it the right way round.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Slide the brass plate over the letter, read it, then tap the bearings on the dial in order.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: That is not what the letter says. Read it again through the plate.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Order matters on a compass dial. Check each bearing.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A brass key. Small enough to fit a drawer in his desk.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: A spare lens. Aurelio loved looking closely at things.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A folded scrap of map with only coastlines and no names at all.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: This globe has no names either. Every world here was erased on purpose.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Faint pencil marks along the edge. Something was rubbed out here.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: My reflection is backwards. Maybe the letter is meant to be read this way.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The key turned! There is a letter inside, but the writing is reversed.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The Sky Dock! My kind of place. That gear housing is a compass engine.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Then the crank must turn the compass gear. Some gears are missing from the pegs.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The compass gear is turning! Right way, right speed, and the whole dock hums.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Aurelio left another clue: the Moon is never first or last. Into the Logbook it goes.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Each number between pegs is the sum of the two gears' teeth. The crank has 12, and the compass gear must have 24.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Start at the compass: the number beside it minus 24 gives its neighbour. Work back along the links to the crank.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: That layout does not work yet. Look at which gears really touch.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Gears that overlap jam. Gears that do not touch do not turn.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Oil! Everything on an airship runs better with a little oil.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A mooring chart. It shows the dock, but the sea around it is blank.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: A storm flag, torn at the edge. The wind up here has stories.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The note on the bench says gears touch only when their teeth add up to the number engraved on the link.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The hull plate says a double-size gear turns half as fast, so the compass gear must have twice the crank's teeth.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Oiled! The crank spins smoothly now.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The observatory dome. It is dark, but the stars on the wall chart still wait.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: We will need a light to find them. A real one, not just a flashlight.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The stars are joined! The dome opens a little, and a stair appears.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Aurelio says the Key comes before the Anchor. Another page for the Logbook.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Light the lantern, then drag its glow around the dome until every star shows.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The chart says brightest to faintest. The biggest stars are the brightest.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Not that star. The next one should be a little smaller than the last.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Start at the biggest star and work down to the smallest.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: A box of matches, still dry. The lantern will love these.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A lens cap from the telescope. Aurelio was careful with his things.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Brass dividers, for measuring the gaps between stars on a chart.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The chart says: join the stars from the brightest to the faintest.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: A star globe. The dots on it come in different sizes, just like in the sky.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The lantern is lit! Its glow can search the whole dome.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Through the eyepiece I can see the moon. Something is scratched on the rim.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The Heart Chamber. The compass floats, and the islands outside have no names.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Six stones, but seven glyphs on the lock. We must be careful.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The compass is awake! Every forgotten world is drifting closer to the windows.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Aurelio left the choice to us. The worlds can return, or stay safe in the dark.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Use the three clues in the Logbook: what is left out, what is never first or last, what comes before what.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: After each try, a filled pip means the right place. A hollow pip means the right glyph, wrong place.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The lock resets after six tries. Think about what we already know.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: The rose wants the three bearings from Aurelio's letter. Check the Logbook.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A silver shard from an island. It hums like a tuning fork.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Aurelio's signet ring! He stood right here, at the heart of his house.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: A drop of cloud glass. Inside, a tiny island turns slowly.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The rim says: a filled pip for the right place, a hollow ring for the right glyph elsewhere.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Aurelio wrote: keep the three bearings from my study letter. The rose will ask for them.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: The Eye stone is cracked. Something is hidden in the crack.

dialogue.speaker: aurelio
dialogue.text: Well done, my apprentice. The worlds are awake. A map is only ink; what you draw on it, you decide.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Then let them be drawn again. Every one of them, with their own names.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: Look at the needle! It is swinging toward a world with no name at all.

dialogue.speaker: tamsin
dialogue.text: Some worlds are safest when they sleep. We will keep their secret, Aurelio.

dialogue.speaker: corvin
dialogue.text: And the compass stays ours, ready if they ever call.

brasskey.name: Brass Key
brasskey.text: A small brass key with a compass rose cut into its bow. It fits a drawer in the study desk.

lens.name: Spare Lens
lens.text: A round lens in a brass ring. Aurelio kept one for every map he ever studied.

mapscrap.name: Folded Map Scrap
mapscrap.text: A scrap of coastline with every name scraped away. Only the compass rose survived.

oilcan.name: Oil Can
oilcan.text: The label reads: "Oil every mesh. Gears that touch turn opposite ways." A dented little can for a stiff crank.

moorchart.name: Mooring Chart
moorchart.text: A sketch of the gear housing: the crank gear has 12 teeth and the compass gear needs 24. Along each link between pegs a number is written.

stormflag.name: Storm Flag
stormflag.text: A rust-orange flag with a note stitched on: "A gear that touches nothing turns nothing." Torn by many winds.

matches.name: Matchbox
matches.text: A box of long matches, still dry. Good for lighting a lantern.

lenscap.name: Lens Cap
lenscap.text: The brass cap of the great telescope. Engraved with a tiny star.

dividers.name: Brass Dividers
dividers.text: Dividers for measuring the gaps between stars on a chart.

signet.name: Aurelio's Signet
signet.text: A silver ring stamped with a compass rose. It is still warm, as if he only just left.

shard.name: Silver Island Shard
shard.text: A sliver of floating island that hums softly, like a tuning fork.

cloudglass.name: Cloud Glass
cloudglass.text: A drop of glass with a tiny island turning slowly inside.

truths: Aurelio's letter: set the rose to West, then South, then East.
The Eye and the Flame are not in the code.
The Moon is never first or last.
The Key comes before the Anchor.
The compass is awake. The forgotten worlds can be seen again.

r1.help: Slide the brass plate over Aurelio's letter to read it, then set the dial.

dial.help: Tap the bearings in the order the letter gives.
dial.wrongText: The dial does not move. Read the letter again.

r2.help: Each number on the dashed links is the two gears' tooth counts added together. Tap a spare gear, then a peg. Tap a placed gear to take it off.
r2.goal: Crank = 12 teeth. The compass gear must turn the same way, once for every two crank turns.

r3.help: Drag the lantern across the dark dome to light every star.
r3.joinHelp: All seven stars are lit. Join them from the brightest to the faintest.

stages.title: The glyph lock
stages.help: Choose four different glyphs. Use the three clues in your Logbook.

stages.title: The rose
stages.help: Set the compass rose to the three bearings from Aurelio's letter. Look in your Logbook.
stages.wrongText: The rose does not turn. Check the Logbook.

rooms.name: Map House Study
rooms.objective: Find Aurelio's letter and set the compass dial.
rooms.objectiveReady: Read the letter in the brass plate, then set the dial.

hotspots.label: Blank globe
hotspots.title: The blank globe
hotspots.text: Every land is bare and every ocean is painted over in grey. Only a tiny compass rose is etched at the foot of the stand: Aurelio's mark.

hotspots.label: Rubbed-out map
hotspots.title: Pencil marks on the map
hotspots.text: Along the edge, a row of rubbed-out names. Beside them Aurelio wrote: "Erased from the maps, not from the world."

hotspots.label: Brass plate
hotspots.title: The brass plate
views: The plate is polished like a mirror. Your reflection looks back at you, with left and right swapped.

Engraved around the rim:
READ ME AS I AM IN THE PLATE.
hotspots.secret: Whatever is reversed in ink is true in brass.

rooms.name: Sky Dock Loft
rooms.objective: Wake the compass engine in the gear housing.
rooms.objectiveReady: Place the spare gears so the crank turns the compass gear.

reward.toast: The gangway lowers into the clouds.

hotspots.label: Gear bench
hotspots.title: The gear bench
hotspots.text: A note pinned among the cogs: "Two gears touch only when their tooth counts add up to the number engraved on the link between their pegs. A gear that touches nothing turns nothing."

hotspots.label: Airship hull plate
hotspots.title: The hull plate
hotspots.text: Stamped on the hull plate: "A gear twice as big turns half as fast. The compass gear must have DOUBLE the crank's teeth. Gears that touch turn opposite ways, so count the links: an even number keeps the turn the same."

rooms.name: Observatory Dome
rooms.objective: Light the dome and find the stars.
rooms.objectiveReady: Sweep the dome with the lantern, then join the stars.

reward.toast: A stair unfolds from the dome wall.

hotspots.label: Wall star chart
hotspots.title: The wall star chart
hotspots.text: Under the chart, in Aurelio's hand: "Join the stars from the brightest to the faintest."

hotspots.label: Star globe
hotspots.title: The star globe
hotspots.text: The stars on this globe are dots of many sizes. Big dots are bright stars, small dots are faint ones.

hotspots.label: Telescope eyepiece
hotspots.title: The eyepiece
views: Through the eyepiece: a pale moon, sharp as a coin, with storm clouds drifting across it.
Scratched around the eyepiece rim, small and neat: a ring of tiny stars.
hotspots.secret: Light shows what the dark keeps. Bigger means brighter.

rooms.name: Heart Chamber
rooms.objectiveReady: Crack the glyph lock, then set the rose.

hotspots.label: Engraved floor rim
hotspots.title: The engraved rim
hotspots.text: Around the floor ring: "A filled pip for the right place. A hollow ring for the right glyph in the wrong place. Six turns, then the lock forgets."

hotspots.label: Pillar note
hotspots.title: Aurelio's note on the pillar
hotspots.text: "Keep the three bearings from my study letter. The rose will ask for them. Read them back from your Logbook."

hotspots.label: Eye stone
hotspots.title: The Eye stone
views: The Eye stone stands cracked and mossy. Six stones circle the lock, but the lock knows seven glyphs.
In the crack, under the moss: a tiny scratched glyph.
hotspots.secret: A small Star is scratched here. The seventh glyph has no stone.

cinematic: The last bearing is set. The great compass turns, and the windows of the Heart Chamber fill with islands no map has ever drawn.

choose.prompt: What will Tamsin do with the forgotten worlds?

options.label: Restore the forgotten worlds to the map
cinematic: Tamsin lays her pen on the great chart. Name by name, coast by coast, the erased worlds return to the paper.
The brass needle trembles, swings away from every known place, and settles on a world with no name at all. A new voyage waits.

win.title: The Map Remembers
win.text: The forgotten worlds are back on the map. And the compass already points at one more, a world nobody has named yet.

options.label: Leave them forgotten and safe
cinematic: Tamsin folds the blank chart and closes the compass. Outside, the islands drift quietly back into the clouds.
Some worlds are kept best by those who know where they are, and say nothing.

win.title: The Quiet Map
win.text: The forgotten worlds sleep on, safe and secret, and the Map House stands dry above the tide.

timeup.title: The Tide Rises
timeup.text: The storm tide floods the Map House, and the compass goes dark. Aurelio's secret sinks with it.
